steps.title: In the ground
steps.text: Strontium is mined as celestite, a pale blue-white strontium sulphate that forms in beds where ancient seas and lakes dried out. Iran, Spain and China mine nearly all of it.

steps.title: Mine and sort
steps.text: Celestite is quarried from open pits. The ore is rich, so it needs little more than crushing, washing and sorting to reach saleable grade.

steps.title: Convert
steps.text: Celestite does not dissolve, so it is roasted with coal in a rotating kiln at about 1,100°C. This turns it into strontium sulphide, which does. The sulphide is leached with water and treated with carbon dioxide or soda ash, and strontium carbonate settles out.
steps.india: Vishnu Chemicals has close to 10,000 tonnes a year of carbonate capacity, about half of it in use in mid-2026, running on imported ore.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Carbonate is fired with iron oxide into strontium ferrite, a black ceramic magnet. It is also dissolved in nitric acid to make strontium nitrate.
steps.india: Sold mainly to makers of flexible magnets.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Ferrite magnets are the cheap, everyday magnets in small motors, loudspeakers and fridge seals. Strontium nitrate burns brilliant red in fireworks and signal flares. Ground celestite weights the drilling mud in oil wells, and a trace of strontium refines aluminium castings.
